findings.seam: S6/S7 (scripts/tickets_dispatch_launch.py) x contracts/dispatch.md -- the landed prompt against the claim its contract still makes
findings.summary: The run knowingly leaves contracts/dispatch.md's enumeration two facts short of the prompt it describes, on the stated ground that changing it would be a forbidden T0 shape change. It would not have been. The refusal that actually fires for that edit is the routine hash-pin mismatch, whose own error message names --pin as the remedy; the T0-shape refusal -- the one the standing constraint forbids -- is a different check that this edit never reaches. I concur with the outcome (a unit re-pinning a repo-wide contract hash on its own authority is the wrong shape) and not with the reason, and the reason is the part that will repeat.
findings.evidence: contracts/dispatch.md:80-87 reads "The prompt names, once each, ... the resolved pack craft, the review lane's root ticket path, the assigned name, ... and that every check runs to completion in the turn it starts." At the tip the prompt also names the applied skill's own resolved file (scripts/tickets_dispatch_launch.py:264-283, _identity_line), and its check sentence reads "...in the turn it starts, with an explicit timeout longer than the check; never background a gate or a test run, kill anything you background once it is superseded, and never report a check you did not watch finish" (ibid. :466-469). Neither is in the enumeration. I reproduced the refusal rather than trusting the report: copied contracts/ + tools/validate.py + tools/validate_support/ + scripts/doclint.py + tests/pins.json into a temp tree, applied both edits to the copy, and ran tools/validate.py against it -- exit 1, and the single dispatch.md line is `ERROR contracts/dispatch.md: T0 contract changed; if intentional, re-pin via: python tools/validate.py --pin`. That string is tools/validate_support/packages.py:47. The shape refusal is a different check: tools/validate_support/lint.py:134-155, docstring "Refuse a T0 shape re-pin without a record citing the old pin", which fires only on a named-field or enum change (T0_FIELD_RE at :95 matches backticked lowercase field names, T0_TABLE_FIELD_RE at :96 matches table field cells) and demands a `T0 supersess... sha256:<old digest>` record. A prose clause added to a paragraph matches neither pattern, so lint.py:134 never fired here. The pin is a plain digest: tests/pins.json:2, "dispatch.md": "1d7acee1a635...".
findings.cause: Two distinct refusals share the token T0, and the work order's standing constraint names only one of them: "no T0 shape change -- if a unit appears to need one, stop and hand back." B1.5 met a message that says `T0 contract changed`, read it as the constraint it had been given, and stopped -- correctly, by the letter of its instruction. The frame then endorsed the reading verbatim ("which is exactly the standing constraint"). Nobody re-read the refusal to see which check emitted it. The same conflation will stop the next unit that edits any contract prose, because every such edit produces that identical message.
findings.remedy: Two parts, both small. (1) Close the drift: one `python tools/validate.py --pin` at the join or by the user, taken together with adding the applied skill's resolved file to the :80-87 enumeration and extending its check item to name the timeout and the supersession kill. The neighbouring sentence "It names no skill for the child to invoke and no pack for it to resolve: it hands the paths" became MORE true with S7 and needs no change -- the frame is right about that, and it is why this is drift in the enumeration and not in the law. (2) Extinguish the class: the standing-constraint wording in the next work order should say "no T0 SHAPE change (a named field or enum, refused by tools/validate_support/lint.py with a supersession demand); a plain hash re-pin, which validate.py itself prescribes as --pin, is mechanical and is the coordinator's to take." One sentence, and it un-blocks every future contract-prose edit.

findings.seam: S2 (B1.4) -- the document-tree branch of _return_lines, and what the same change removed from the same prompt
findings.summary: F4's repair left the git-shaped noun behind. A content-pack child is now told "Commit your work inside this candidate before you close" -- but the same commit's adapter comment states that a document-tree child "commits straight onto the coordinator's own branch, so it must commit but has no isolated candidate for land to merge." The word candidate then occurs exactly once in the entire 477-word prompt, with no antecedent anywhere in it, because the one line that used to describe this lane's workspace -- the pack craft's ## Workspace channel sentence -- was the else-branch payload and is no longer rendered for this pack at all. The instruction's imperative is right and the child will do the right thing; the noun it acts on does not exist.
findings.evidence: Rendered through the real composer, not read from a transcript: launch_prompt over all five packs with each pack's own declared cells (exit 0). orch-content-pack (commits_in_place=True, git_candidate=False) yields 477 words, prompt.count("candidate") == 1, prompt.count("Commit your work inside this candidate") == 1, and no ## Workspace line. orch-code/design/data-pack yield count("candidate") == 2 -- the clause plus "the landing merges the candidate" -- so the noun has a referent only where a candidate exists. orch-research-pack yields count("candidate") == 0 and keeps its workspace line. The contradicted claim is scripts/tickets_adapters.py:33-40, added by this same unit. docs/vocabulary.md:233 defines the term as "candidate worktree -- the derived tree an isolation-required item works in"; a document-tree lane is not isolation-required (scripts/tickets_assignment.py:88, required = derived_isolation(...) == "required", is False for it, which is why workspace_establishment_finding returns None and the lane records branch and baseline as None). The removal is visible in the test diff: tests/test_ticket_callables.py:377 previously asserted assertIn(_workspace_line(craft_path(DOC_PACK)), prompt); that assertion is gone and nothing replaced it, so no check now pins that a document-tree child is told anything at all about its workspace. The frame recorded the removal as "a consequence worth recording, not a defect" and did not connect it to the retained noun.
findings.cause: _return_lines was split by CONDITION and not by SENTENCE. B1.4 correctly made the merge sentence conditional on git_candidate while leaving the first sentence a single literal shared by both branches -- and that literal was authored for the git lane, where "this candidate" is the established worktree. The pack's own workspace sentence, which would have supplied the missing referent, sat in the else-branch the new condition now skips, so one change removed the antecedent at the same moment it started needing one.
findings.remedy: One branch on the cell the function already reads, no new cell and no new surface: where git_candidate is false, say "Commit your work in the tree you are standing in" (or "in this workspace") instead of "inside this candidate", exactly as the merge sentence is already chosen two lines above. Optionally, and separately, keep the pack's ## Workspace channel line for a commits_in_place-and-not-git_candidate lane, so section-overlap conflict semantics reach the child from the prompt as well as from the craft it is told to read -- that is a budget question for the prompt's owner, and the noun fix does not depend on it. Pin it where the family already pins the rest: tests/test_dispatch_launch.py:230 asserts this sentence for this pack today and would carry the new wording for free.

findings.seam: S1 (B1.1 x B1.6) -- the acceptance grep's spelling against the fact it was meant to enumerate
findings.summary: S1's acceptance -- "a repo-wide grep for the walk idiom finds the owner plus only sites carrying the documented exception comment" -- holds for the test trees after B1.6, and does not hold for production. Exactly two live sites derive the repository root, carry no exception comment, and were never in scope, because the acceptance was specified by SPELLING (resolve().parents[ and its variants) rather than by MEANING (does this expression evaluate to the repository root?). Both were named honestly in B1.1's own report and neither was carried forward by any later ticket, while the frame's close records only that the test-tree half now holds.
findings.evidence: I classified semantically instead of by spelling: for every tracked *.py outside tests/ and reader/tests/, evaluate each Path(__file__).resolve() walk from the file's real path and keep only those equal to the repository root. Result, exit 0: 24 production sites resolve to the root; 22 carry an explanatory comment in the eight lines above; the remainder are scripts/_bootstrap.py:25 (the owner, documented as such at :22-24) and install.py:67, `_LOCAL_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent` -- a single .parent because install.py sits AT the root, so `parents[` never matched it. A second site the same blindness hides is reader/tools/ui_frontend.py:21, `REPOSITORY_ROOT = ROOT.parent`, chained off an already-resolved name rather than off Path(__file__).resolve() at all. git diff --stat 31b85fc7 e572cc47 -- install.py reader/tools/ui_frontend.py is EMPTY (exit 0), so neither was touched. B1.1's report names both explicitly (on installer/foundation.py: install.py's _LOCAL_ROOT is "a single .resolve().parent, one level shallower, so it never matched the grep pattern itself"; and in its Checks-run section on ui_frontend.py: "a repo-root derivation via a different idiom than the ones enumerated -- it never matched the specified grep spellings"). The frame graded B1.1 limited for the test tree and, after B1.6, wrote "S1's test-tree acceptance now holds" -- true, and silent about production.
findings.cause: An acceptance stated as a grep pattern grades the pattern, not the fact. Any site whose depth is 1, or whose walk is chained off a name resolved on an earlier line, is invisible to resolve().parents[ and resolve().parent.parent no matter how many spellings are added -- the enumeration is unbounded in exactly the direction the defect lives. This is the run's recurring shape once more (S3's mutant graded the sentences already fixed; the prior run's B1.8 word-boundary grep was blind to identifiers), with the same signature: the oracle and the goal are written in different languages.
findings.remedy: Two comments -- install.py:67 stating that this line is what puts the root on sys.path, so it cannot read the fact it establishes; reader/tools/ui_frontend.py:21 stating that this file is run with working-directory reader and derives the reader root first. Then, to extinguish the class rather than the instance, state the acceptance semantically and ship the classifier as the check: evaluate every Path(__file__) walk in the tree from its own file's path and assert that each site resolving to the repository root is the owner or carries a comment. It is about 25 lines and it is exactly the check that found these two.

findings.seam: S1 (B1.1) -- the justifying comment left at tools/validate_support/common.py against the module's actual importers
findings.summary: The comment B1.1 wrote to justify converging this module claims tools/validate.py is "the only entry point that loads this module." It is not: four test modules import tools.validate_support.* directly, and both packages.py and duplication.py import common at their own module scope, so importing any of them loads it. The comment's conclusion (the import is safe) is correct and I verified it; its premise, which is the part a later reader will rely on when deciding whether some other caller is allowed, is false. Same defect shape as F3 itself and as the one the frame's own join commit e572cc47 repaired -- prose asserting something about the code beside it that is not true of that code.
findings.evidence: tools/validate_support/common.py:13-17 (added by this run): "tools/validate.py, the only entry point that loads this module, has already put the repository root on sys.path before importing anything under tools.validate_support -- so this leaf import needs no walk of its own". Direct importers of the package, from git grep -nE validate_support -- '*.py' with the package's own files excluded: tests/test_browser_game_traceability.py:11-12, tests/test_fact_registry.py:26, tests/test_run_required.py:515, tests/test_validate_cases/contract_pins.py:24. That those reach common is not inference: tools/validate_support/packages.py:5 and duplication.py:10 both begin `from tools.validate_support import common as __dep_common`, and running python -c with only '.' inserted on sys.path and `import tools.validate_support.packages` prints `common loaded: True` with ROOT equal to this workspace (exit 0), tools/validate.py never executed. I also probed whether the change made anything newly fragile and it did not: rebuilding the temp tree that tests/test_validator_cases/repo_and_frontmatter.py builds and running validate.py in it with cwd set to the temp tree fails at `import doclint` -> `import console`, a pre-existing cwd dependency older than this run; with cwd at the repository root (what the test actually does) it exits 0 and writes pins. So this is a comment finding and not a behavior finding.
findings.cause: The convergence needed a per-site justification, and the justification was written from the site's PRIMARY caller rather than from its importers. tools/validate.py is the only PRODUCTION entry point, which is what B1.1 verified; "only entry point" then got written where "only production entry point, and every other importer already has the root on sys.path for the same reason" was meant. Nothing checks a justifying comment against the import graph it describes, so the error is invisible to every check in the tree.
findings.remedy: One sentence at the site: "Every entry point that loads this module -- tools/validate.py, and the test modules that import tools.validate_support.* directly -- already has the repository root on sys.path, so this leaf import needs no walk of its own." The same edit is worth checking at tools/validate_measures_support/common.py:8-11, whose "this module's only importer" claim I did verify true (tools/validate_measures.py is its only importer, git grep exit 0).

findings.seam: S3 (B1.3, repaired by B1.6) -- the residue of wrap-fragility the whole-file reflow mutant does not reach, and the negative guard beside it
findings.summary: The positive pins in CritiqueContractTest are now whitespace-insensitive, and the frame's width-58 whole-file reflow passes. Swept across 81 widths instead of one, five of them still fail -- and the third test in the same class, which no width sweep covers because it asserts absence, is not normalized at all, so a wrap through its one multi-word phrase makes it silently pass. That last one is a false GREEN, a worse failure mode than the false RED S3 was written to remove.
findings.evidence: Taken without mutating the tree -- the pins were replayed against an in-memory reflow of skills/kernel/orch-judge/SKILL.md, so no file was written and git status --short stayed empty (exit 0). Across widths 30..110 with textwrap.fill at its defaults, the eight normalized pins fail at exactly five widths -- 30, 43, 44, 82, 83 -- always on the same pin, "A critique enumerates evidence-backed findings". The cause is visible in the width-30 output: `critique enumerates evidence-` / `backed findings, then`. Re-run with break_on_hyphens=False: 0 of 81 widths fail. For contrast the pre-S3 form (no normalization) fails at width 58, which is the reading the frame recorded. Separately, tests/test_verification_model.py:78-96, test_live_ticket_review_surfaces_drop_stale_authority_and_oracle_model, asserts assertNotIn over six phrases against the raw joined text of four files; one of them, "named oracle", contains a space. Demonstrated on a copy carrying that phrase across a line break: the assertion PASSES (guard blind); with the same " ".join(text.split()) normalization its two siblings now use, it FIRES.
findings.cause: S3 patched the symptom its mutant could see. textwrap.fill breaks on hyphens by default, so the run's own chosen reflow tool can split a hyphenated compound, and whitespace normalization cannot rejoin `evidence- backed`. Underneath that, the class keeps producing defects because the checks pin raw prose at all: this pack's craft says "Checks pin shapes, never sentences" and "A check reading an owner file reads a stable anchor -- a heading, a backticked name, a fenced command" (packs/orch-code-pack/references/craft.md, ## Shape). Six of the eight pins are bare sentences; the two already robust are the ones carrying backticks. Whitespace normalization lets prose-pinning survive one more class of edit without making it right.
findings.remedy: Smallest fix that removes the false green: normalize joined in test_live_ticket_review_... the way its two siblings normalize -- one line, phrase list unchanged. Smallest fix for the residual false red: either pin a phrase with no hyphenated compound ("enumerates evidence" and "backed findings" are separately unique) or define the reflow mutant as break_on_hyphens=False and say so wherever that acceptance is written down, so the next unit's mutant and the next unit's pin agree. The class remedy is the craft's own rule: move these to anchors -- the ## Lens heading, the backticked findings line, the fenced command -- and let the prose move freely underneath them.

findings.seam: S7 -- the acceptance clause the run structurally defers, and which no ticket now owns
findings.summary: S7 says "Verify post-reinstall on a live run: no unscoped filesystem search in any worker's task list." That observation has not been taken and cannot be taken from this branch as things stand, because the library is installed from main and the change is not merged. The frame recorded the pre-reinstall run as a positive control and said the post-reinstall reading "still has to be taken" -- then the run closed without an owner for it. This is not a defect in the code; it is an acceptance clause with no successor, and this very ticket is first-person evidence of the gap.
findings.evidence: The installed dispatch machinery carries none of this run's work: grep for commits_in_place, "timeout longer than the check" and "whose file is" over C:\Users\danhm\.orchflows\bin\tickets_dispatch_launch.py, tickets_adapters.py and tickets_assignment.py returns 0 matches in all three (exit 1). Consistent with that, this ticket's own launch prompt -- rendered by that installed machinery minutes ago -- opens "Apply skill orch-judge to ticket ..." with no skill file, and its check line reads "Run every check to completion in the turn it starts; never background a gate or a test run, and never report a check you did not watch finish": both pre-S6/S7 forms. So the live surface is still the positive control, not the negative one. I did extend what the frame proved, in the direction that de-risks the deferred reading: rings.resolve("skill", ...) was exercised through the INSTALLED resolver rather than the checkout -- lib_root() returns C:\Users\danhm\.orchflows\lib, and both orch-do and orch-judge resolve to an existing SKILL.md (exit 0). The frame's renders were all from the checkout, where a wrong lib_root would still have found the file. So S7(a)'s carrier will hold post-reinstall; what remains unobserved is only whether the model then stops searching.
findings.cause: The unit's Acceptance sentence and the unit's body ask for different things: the body says "verify post-reinstall on a live run", the Acceptance line says only "the live-run observation is reported" -- which the pre-reinstall positive control satisfies literally. That is this run's recurring shape once more, in the work order rather than in a child: an acceptance whose words can be satisfied without its goal being reached. The frame saw it and said so plainly; nothing in the ticket set could carry a post-merge act, so it fell out at the close.
findings.remedy: No code change. At the join, name the observation as an explicit successor with its own trigger -- "after the merge and reinstall, read the first orch-do child's task list and record whether an unscoped filesystem search appears" -- so it is a queued item rather than a sentence in a closed journal. It costs one line and it is the only half of S7 that no check can take.
